hero.kicker: Mulch installation and flower beds in Fenton, MI
hero.title: Fresh mulch, **crisp edges.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes gets Fenton flower beds back in shape: weeded, edged clean along the lawn, laid with fabric where it helps, and finished in fresh black, brown or red mulch at a depth that does the plants some good.

local.title: Mulch that suits **the ground under it.**
local.intro: A bed on a sandy rise in the city dries out by noon in July. A bed near the lake or the river can stay wet for days. Mulch helps both, if it goes down at the right depth and stays off the stems. Most of what goes wrong with mulch is too much of it, piled too high.

points.title: Two to three inches, not a mountain
points.body: MSU Extension says 2 to 3 inches of mulch is enough to get the full benefit, and a bed that still has last year's needs only about an inch on top. Mulch piled up against a trunk, the volcano look, invites rot and insects.

points.title: Sandy beds hold water better
points.body: On the well drained Boyer and Wawasee soils, mulch keeps the ground cooler and slows drying; an MSU trial found 3 inches of wood chips cut midday soil temperature by 18 degrees. It cuts down on watering but does not replace it.

points.title: Fabric under shrubs, not perennials
points.body: Fabric plus mulch holds weeds down well in shrub beds, according to MSU. In perennial beds, though, roots and weeds grow into it, it is hard to pull out later, and over the years it can slow water soaking in.

points.title: Boxwood is on the watch list
points.body: Michigan's agriculture department confirmed box tree moth in Genesee County in September 2026, found near the edge of the existing quarantine that already covers Oakland and Livingston counties. If your beds have boxwood, we look for webbing and chewed leaves while we work and tell you what we see.

logistics.title: What a bed day looks like.
body: We pull the weeds, cut a clean edge between bed and lawn, and break up old mulch that has caked into a crust, since MSU notes crusted mulch can shed water instead of letting it in. Fabric goes down in shrub beds where you want it. Then fresh mulch goes on, kept back from trunks and off the crowns of perennials, and the walks and drive get blown off.

Rob comes out first, looks at the beds, and gives you a price and a color choice: black, brown or red. If the borders themselves are failing, with old brick sinking into the lawn or timbers rotting, he will say so, and the fix is [new edging or a block wall](/bed-edging-and-block-walls/).

facts.label: MSU depth guide
facts.value: 2 to 3 inches, about 1 inch to top up

faq.q: Do you install mulch in Fenton?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes weeds, edges and mulches flower beds in the City of Fenton and the township, in black, brown or red, with fabric under shrub beds where it helps. When the whole bed needs rethinking, that is [landscaping](/landscaping-fenton-mi/). Call [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040) for a free estimate.

About 2 to 3 inches, according to MSU Extension, and only about an inch on top of a bed that already has some from last year. Deeper is not better: thick layers can smother perennials, encourage rot at the crown and dry into a crust that sheds water.

faq.q: Is landscape fabric worth it under mulch?
faq.a: Under shrubs, usually yes. MSU says fabric plus mulch controls most weeds there in a tidy way. In perennial beds it can become a headache, because roots and weeds grow through it and it is hard to remove later, so we skip it in beds you plan to divide and replant.

faq.q: What should I do if I see webbing on boxwood in Fenton?
faq.a: Look closer and report it. The state says box tree moth caterpillars are green and yellow with white, yellow and black stripes and black spots, and they leave loose webbing and chewed or skeletonized leaves. They feed only on boxwood. Report suspected moths to the Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development before spraying or throwing the plants away.
